writeup: TIC 405215869 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.2517 days. The TESS mission detected a primary eclipse that dims the system by 8.30 percent, with a box least-squares signal-to-noise ratio of 429.8. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirmed the signal at the target location, though with a centroid offset of 2.3 arcsec and a peak signal-to-noise of 15.1. This object does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a new candidate for follow-up observation. The automated pipeline assigned it a machine-learning score of 0.38, and the light curve passed all data quality checks.
